factual_summary: The Key Laboratory for the Structure and Evolution of Celestial Objects, a subsidiary of Yunnan Observatories, was established in December 2012 under the approval of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. exact_title: Researchers Report Dwarf Novae Unlikely to Be Type Ia Supernova Progenitors----Yunnan Observatories
factual_summary: Recently, PhD student LI Ruijie and Prof. WANG Bo from Yunnan Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences, reported new findings on dwarf novae. The team found that cyclic accretion in dwarf novae cannot sustain stable hydrogen burning on white dwarfs. Recurrent nova eruptions reduce the mass retention efficiency of white dwarfs, preventing them from growing to the Chandrasekhar mass limit through long-term accretion. Therefore, dwarf novae are unlikely to be progenitor systems of Type Ia supernovae. The study has been published in the international astronomical journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.

exact_title: Solar Site Survey and Coronal Observation Group----Yunnan Observatories
factual_summary: To advance the technique of ground-based observations and to solve the fundamental problems of solar physics, it is essential that optimum sites be allocated for the purpose of optical and IR solar observations in the near future. The western inland regions of China boast a homogeneous and stable atmosphere, an ample amount of sunlight hours, in addition to a high altitude. exact_title: Study Confirms Compact Companion around the RR Lyrae Star IY Lyr----Yunnan Observatories
factual_summary: Researchers from the Yunnan Observatories (Chinese Academy of Sciences), working with the Ulugh Beg Astronomical Institute of Uzbekistan, have identified a compact companion orbiting the RR Lyrae star IY Lyr. By combining photometric, spectroscopic, and astrometric data—including LAMOST (Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope) spectroscopy, ZTF (Zwicky Transient Facility), TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite), ASAS-SN (All-Sky Automated Survey for Supernovae), and dedicated BVRI observations from the Maidanak 60-cm telescope—they provided the first robust evidence for a companion with a mass of 1.37 solar masses around this RRc-type variable star.

exact_title: Biomaterials and Tissue Engineering--Shanghai Institute of Ceramics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
factual_summary: The Shanghai Institute of Ceramics, Chinese Academy of Sciences has been researching biomedical materials since the 1980s and established the Center of Biomaterials and Tissue Engineering in 2001. Since its establishment, the center has focused on basic and applied research on nanobiomaterials, tissue engineering scaffold materials, biomaterial surfaces and interfaces, and organoid materials and devices. exact_title: Energy Materials--Shanghai Institute of Ceramics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
factual_summary: Center of Energy Materials is mainly engaged in basic research, applied basic research, device construction, and engineering technology research and development of advanced functional materials related to new energy. Focusing on the research fields of solid-state rechargeable battery materials and devices, electrochemical energy storage materials and devices, green optoelectronic conversion technology, light metal-based battery systems and materials, hydrogen energy materials and devices, fuel cell materials, and systems, etc., the center has laid out strategic emerging directions such as solid-state batteries, solar cells, fluorine-based batteries, electrocatalytic hydrogen production, metal-air batteries, sodium-ion batteries, and solid oxide fuel cells. exact_title: State Key Laboratory of High Performance Ceramics--Shanghai Institute of Ceramics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
factual_summary: The State Key Laboratory of High Performance Ceramics and Superfine Microstructure was founded in April 1988 upon the approval of both the State Planning Commission and the Chinese Academy of Sciences, aiming at promoting the high-performance ceramic research activity in China. The laboratory is subject to the Shanghai Institute of Ceramics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and has been open to all over the world since 1989. In 1991, the laboratory formerly became one of the State Key Laboratories and has been given the name since then. In January 2023, the Chinese Academy of Sciences approved the reorganization of the laboratory as the “State Key Laboratory of High Performance Ceramics”. In January 2025, it passed the reorganization evaluation by the Ministry of Science and Technology and was officially established.

factual_summary: At a lab of the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), AI and automation have transformed traditional chemistry research from manual trial-and-error to giving instructions on intelligent platforms. In 2021, Professor Jiang Jun's team developed the first-generation robotic chemist "Xiao Lai," enabling 24/7 operation and autonomous experiment design. The team's ultimate goal is fully autonomous science, where machines can discover new research directions and assist even non-experts in material creation. (Xinhua)

exact_title: Advanced Semiconductor Science Program (ASSP) | RIKEN
factual_summary: As the technology for generative AI develops and its use expands dramatically, reducing energy consumption has become an urgent issue. In order to achieve ultra-low power consumption for AI servers, technological innovation is required for the semiconductor devices used in generative AI. The Advanced Semiconductor Science Program (ASSP) promotes the design and development of semiconductor devices that can be used in next-generation supercomputing infrastructures, integrated device for advanced computational science, and the foundation for new science, such as quantum innovation, in collaboration with various research centers within RIKEN. In addition, we aim to reduce the cost of design and apply it to edge AI through collaboration with universities and companies in Japan and overseas.

exact_title: ECL Unit Leader Leo Speidel elected a 2026 AYS Fellow in Life Sciences | RIKEN
factual_summary: Leo Speidel, a RIKEN ECL Unit Leader at the RIKEN Center for Interdisciplinary Theoretical and Mathematical Sciences (iTHEMS) and RIKEN Pioneering Research Institute(PRI) , has been elected as a 2026 Asian Young Scientist (AYS) Fellow in Life Sciences. AYSF is a privately funded research fellowship that aims to encourage and support young scientists in Asia to carry out creative and transformative research. The Fellowship annually selects early-career scientists in three fundamental disciplines: 1) Life Science, 2) Physical Science, and 3) Mathematics and Computer Science. Speidel’s research focuses on the development and application of new mathematical and statistical techniques to reveal human evolution, with the goal of reconstructing genome-wide genealogies across individuals and species. He was selected for this year’s AYSF in recognition of his pioneering achievements.

exact_title: RIKEN establishes innovation company | RIKEN
factual_summary: On September 5, RIKEN established a fully-owned subsidiary, RIKEN Innovation, Co., Ltd., which will work to improve communication between private industry and RIKEN, and to support collaborative projects. This move was made possible by a new law passed in January of this year which allows National Research and Development Institutes such as RIKEN to establish subsidiaries to carry out work related to licensing technologies and conducting joint research with the private sector. Starting on December 1, the new company began carrying out business on behalf of RIKEN. Simultaneously, RIKEN's Cluster for Innovation, which previously handled such work, was shut down.

exact_title: Introduction of Research Laboratory ㅣ AI Safety Institute ㅣ Organization ㅣ Welcome to ETRI
factual_summary: The Korea Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute (Korea AISI) is an organization dedicated to evaluating the risks associated with AI models or systems and researching technologies for preventing and mitigating those risks. We represent the Republic of Korea in collaborating with AI safety research institutes and related organizations worldwide. Established in November 2024, the Korea AISI is committed to fostering an environment conducive to the development and application of safe AI, empowering Korean AI companies to enhance their competitiveness and expand globally, while strengthening international solidarity and standards for AI safety.

exact_title: AMOC : vers des projections climatiques plus fiables grâce aux statistiques | Inria
factual_summary: L’AMOC ( atlantic meridional overturning circulation ) est un vaste système de courants océaniques qui joue un rôle essentiel dans la régulation du climat terrestre. Souvent associé au gulf stream, il désigne en réalité un ensemble de circulations qui transportent des masses d’eau chaude vers l’Atlantique Nord. En atteignant les régions subarctiques, ces eaux se refroidissent, deviennent plus denses et plongent vers les profondeurs avant de se diriger vers l’océan Austral ou elle refond surface. Ce mécanisme constitue l’un des moteurs majeurs de la circulation océanique mondiale.

exact_title: DATASHAPE | Inria
factual_summary: DataShape is a research project in Topological Data Analysis (TDA), a recent field whose aim is to uncover, understand and exploit the topological and geometric structure underlying complex and possibly high dimensional data. The DataShape project gathers a unique variety of expertise that allows it to embrace the mathematical, statistical, algorithmic and applied aspects of the field in a common framework ranging from fundamental theoretical studies to experimental research and software development. The expected output of DataShape is two-fold. First, we intend to set-up and develop the mathematical, statistical and algorithmic foundations of Topological and Geometric Data Analysis. Second, we intend to develop the Gudhi platform in order to provide an efficient state-of-the-art toolbox for the understanding of the topology and geometry of data.

exact_title: 2.1 Introduction
factual_summary: Le processus d’élaboration et de mise en œuvre d’un PAQ comporte cinq phases. exact_title: 2.2 Phase I – Demande
factual_summary: Le candidat désireux d’établir un PAQ doit commencer par envoyer une lettre à l’Inspecteur principal de l’exploitation (IPE) pour lui notifier son intention. Dans sa lettre de réponse, Transports Canada demandera à l’exploitant d’organiser une réunion avec des représentants de son département de la formation. La réunion comprendra l’IPE, un représentant de la Direction des opérations nationales ou d’une division régionale affectée à la surveillance opérationnelle (selon le cas), un expert des flottes aériennes en question (EM), un instructeur (selon le cas) et l’exploitant aérien en personne.

factual_summary: We consider estimating the discretization error in a nonlinear functional J(u) in the setting of an abstract variational problem: find u∈V such that B(u,φ)=L(φ)∀φ∈V, as approximated by a Galerkin finite element method. Here, V is a Hilbert space, B(⋅,⋅) is a bilinear form, and L(⋅) is a linear functional. We consider well-known error estimates η of the form J(u)−J(uh)≈η=L(z)−B(uh,z), where uh denotes a finite element approximation to u, and z denotes the solution to an auxiliary adjoint variational problem. We show that there exist nonlinear functionals for which error estimates of this form are not reliable, even in the presence of an exact adjoint solution z. An estimate η is said to be reliable if there exists a constant C∈R>0 independent of uh such that |J(u)−J(uh)|≤C|η|.
